newsitem.title: GERMANY: Court rejects stores' claim for shock Benetton ads.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects stores' claim for shock Benetton ads.

text.p: A German court has decided that local Benetton retailers are not entitled to compensation for losses in turnover they blamed on the company's shock-style advertising campaign of the early 1990s.

The Federal Court of Justice on Wednesday threw out cases against the Italian clothing group brought by two franchise operators who said their sales had suffered due to the company's controversial "Suffering of the World" campaign.

The ads featured graphic photographs of dead Bosnian soldiers, oil-soaked sea birds and AIDS patients with their families, and prokoved public uproar and even violent attacks against some Benetton shops.
"The decision about the type and intensity of advertising is Benetton's alone, the retailers do not have the ability to influence advertising," the court said in its decision.
"Because of this, Benetton has an obligation to consider the interests of retailers in its business decisions," the court wrote.
"This does not mean, in the view of the court, that Benetton is required in its business policies, and especially not its its advertising, to limit itself to conventional and time-tested methods."

The court added that the company was only obliged to cancel the controversial campaign only when it was "objectively recognisable" that the advertising could hurt retailers, which it said was not apparent until the spring of 1994.
Two months later, Benetton ended the campaign, the court said.
